subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should startup cleanup reclaim legacy/no-starttime current-PID session locks, or should the remaining self-PID recovery policy move under the broader run-lifecycle reliability design?
rationale: The safe fix depends on maintainer intent because reclaiming live Gateway-owned transcript locks can unblock wedged sessions but can also break mutual exclusion if a lock is still legitimately held.

options.title: Keep focused issue open
options.body: Track the legacy/no-starttime startup cleanup gap here while coordinating with the broader live-lock work.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle umbrella
options.body: Move the remaining policy decision to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101863 and close this only after that issue explicitly owns the self-PID lock boundary.

options.title: Accept current conservative behavior
options.body: Treat matching-starttime cleanup as sufficient and document that no-starttime or live-holder locks require doctor/restart lifecycle handling elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Keep focused issue open
recommendation.body: Track the legacy/no-starttime startup cleanup gap here while coordinating with the broader live-lock work.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current routing signal is recent session-lock maintenance and stale-lock policy work in the implicated files.
